title: Sequence-Level Scene + Shared-Hand-Anatomy Focal Refinement
primary_question: Does adding sequence-specific shared hand anatomy and a generic anatomical prior to a scene-based sequence focal estimate improve focal error, absolute wrist/root 3D error and absolute MPJPE, versus scene-only?

scene_branch.aggregation: exp(median(log f_i)) over the unit's scene frames
scene_branch.nuisance: the scene estimator's own principal point is used; no GT cx/cy, k1/k2 or fy/fx ratio enters inference

hand_branch.observations: target-camera monocular WiLoR: keypoints_2d (original pixels) and root-relative keypoints_3d
hand_branch.bone_lengths_from_network: DISCARDED - only unit directions are used
hand_branch.solver: CAM-EXP-009.1 convention: UNDISTORT_ONCE_INTERNAL, 32 alternating iterations, deterministic init
hand_branch.held_out: deterministic FIT/EVAL frame split by SHA-256 bucket

frames.selection: evenly spaced by frame index; never by performance

regularisers.selected_on: SYNTHETIC gate only, never on the real reference focal

compute.N64_DECISION: SKIPPED. Decided from measured runtime BEFORE any focal result: caching 64 hand frames per side would double the inference and the per-unit solver cost, and the solver cost scales with frames x 81 candidates x 2 sides. N=32 remains PRIMARY and 8/16 remain secondary, exactly as specified. This condition is NOT removed after seeing a result.
compute.CONTROL_SCOPE_DECISION: C_WRONG_BONE is run for M3_SCENE_SHARED_GENERIC_FULL ONLY. Decided from measured runtime BEFORE any real focal result: running the control for all three hand variants would roughly double total compute to ~6.2 h. The control's purpose is to test whether the FULL method's hand score uses real anatomical bone correspondence, which M3 alone answers. No condition is removed after seeing a result.
